messages.subject: Hardware requirements
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
I am new to natverse and trying to decide what machine to use to make the most out of it. I will mainly use nat, nblast, and possibly some of the other packages (catmaid?). I currently have a relatively new macbook pro but was wondering if something more powerful might be required, especially in terms of GPU for 3D plotting and interactions with rgl?
Many thanks in advance for your help,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Hardware requirements
messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent,

A new MacBook Pro will be great for plotting and general analysis. The only thing that may cause a problem is memory if you are trying to do large amounts of NBLAST using the parallel option. When NBLASTing all 25,000 hemibrain neurons vs each other, usage is order 20-30 GB per parallel core. Naturally there are ways to improve the memory efficiency but it's one of those things on the long todo …

Note that this is only a concern if you plan to do all by all NBLAST. If you are querying a single or a few neurons against a big database of neurons it's not a problem. If you do want to do all by all NBLAST on many neurons, RAM is the main issue – I would go for 256 GB and up i.e. a workstation or server. But I would not do that until you have a demonstrated need.

In fact RAM is the only really limiting resource in my experience. I have a 32GB RAM MBP and there are occasionally times when I am doing very large analyses where I would like to have 64 GB.

In terms of OS, although the natverse is cross platform it is developed on mac/unix and tested on linux; Windows support for some of the more experimental features sometimes lags.

Final point since you mention Macs, we haven't yet tried the natverse on Apple M1 ARM hardware. It is likely to work fine under the rosetta translation, but it may be some months before native ARM versions of R and all the relevant packages are available.

All the best,

Greg.

messages.body_plain:

Specifically, we are having issues downloading neurons/skeletons. examples: running: `neuprint_read_neurons(544021095)` returns: `Error in neuprint_read_neurons(544021095) : Error reading bodyids` and running:` neuprint_read_skeletons(544021095)` returns: ```Error: neuPrint error: 502 Bad Gateway

502 Bad Gateway

nginx/1.10.3
``` When changing the R environment file to access V1.2 instead everything works fine. We are able to access V1.2, V1.1, V1.01 via the Python API just fine. best, Pasha

messages.subject: Issue with write.im3d
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

i've been having some issues with the write.im3d function. I have read neurons into R and transformed them to various brain registrations. I'm now looking to convert these to .nrrd files, but have been getting an unexpected error which I haven't been able to solve:

neuron <- neuprint_read_neurons(5813046951, heal = TRUE, heal.threshold = 1e9, connectors=FALSE)
neuron.JRC2018U <- xform_brain(neuron*8/1000, reference=JRC2018U, sample="JRCFIB2018F")
im <- as.im3d(xyzmatrix(neuron.JRC2018U), JRC2018U)
write.im3d(im, "5813011145.nrrd")

with this code, I get the error message:
Error in writeBin(as.vector(x, mode = dmode), fc, size = dtypesize, endian = endian) :
  only 2^31-1 bytes can be written in a single writeBin() call

This error occurs while testing a number of other neurons. I've also tried using write.nrrd but I still get the error.

Does anyone have any ideas on what might be causing the error and how to work around it? Would be very grateful for the help.

Thanks,
Rory

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Issue with write.im3d
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rory,

That means that your image dimensions are too large for the current code:

2^31
[1] 2147483648

i.e. ~2GB

> (2^31)^(1/3)
[1] 1290.159

So the limit is about 1290 x 1290 x 1290 or the same product with a different side ratio. I personally have not had to deal with images of this size in R. My first suggestion is to consider slightly increasing your voxel size. If that's not an option then the code needs to be modified. This is the place:

https://github.com/natverse/nat/blob/4d85cc7a2ea66cecd0576c0ff2fe96be722a5341/R/nrrd-io.R#L459-L461

I don't have time to do this just now, but if you want to try and have a go by cloning the nat repo, I think something like the below should work (untested). I'd also recommend making a GitHub issue

https://github.com/natverse/nat/issues

All the best,

Greg.

# add a new function

#' Split slices of an image into chunks based on maximum integer index size
#'
#' @details in R linear indices into arrays can only be 2^31 long (32 bit int).
#'   This means that \code{writeBin} can only write this many pixels in one go.
#'   Therefore to write bigger pixel arrays, you must split the images into chunks
#'   for writing. NB this function currently only works for 3D arrays.
#'
#' @param x An array containing image data
#' @param max_chunk_size (default is max for writeBin)
#'
#' @return a vector of length the number of slices, giving the chunk index (1:nchunks)
#'   for each slice.
make_image_chunks <- function(x, max_chunk_size=2^31-1) {
  lastdim=length(dim(x))
  # FIXME handle arrays that are not 3D
  stopifnot(lastdim==3)
  nslices=dim(x)[lastdim]
  slice_size=prod(dim(x)[-lastdim])
  if(slice_size>max_chunk_size)
    stop("write.nrrd cannot write data with slices with > 2^31 pixels")
  slices_per_chunk=1 + (max_chunk_size %/% slice_size)
  chunk_size=slices_per_chunk * slice_size
  nchunks=1 + nslices %/% slices_per_chunk
  #
  chunks=rep(seq_len(nchunks), rep(slices_per_chunk, nchunks))[seq_len(nslices)]
  chunks
}

# edit these lines:
# https://github.com/natverse/nat/blob/4d85cc7a2ea66cecd0576c0ff2fe96be722a5341/R/nrrd-io.R#L459-L461

fc=ifelse(enc=="gzip", gzfile, base::file)(file, open=fmode)
if(length(x)>=2^31 && max(chunks <- make_image_chunks(x))>1) {
  # too big, must chunk
  for(i in seq_len(max(chunks))) {
    writeBin(as.vector(x[, , chunks == i], mode = dmode),

             fc,
             size = dtypesize,
             endian = endian)
  }

} else {
  # write in one go
  writeBin(as.vector(x, mode=dmode), fc, size=dtypesize, endian=endian)
}
close(fc)

messages.subject: Re: Inquiry regarding NBLAST on-the-fly
messages.body_plain:
Dear Takuro,

Thank you for your message and interest in NBLAST. I am sorry for the
trouble you have been experiencing. The NBLAST server is now run by the
virtual fly brain project. Rob Court, the lead developer, recently had
to do some work on some of the underlying infrastructure and it seems
likely to me that this may be the source of the problem with the server.
Rob, can you provide any insight? I can confirm that I cannot maintain a
stable connection to the server.

As for the desktop install instructions:

http://flybrain.mrc-lmb.cam.ac.uk/si/nblast/www/nblast_desktop/

although they have not been updated for some time, I think they should
work. Have you run into a specific problem? If so, could you please send
a message describing the code that you have run and the error messages
that you observed to:

https://groups.google.com/g/nat-user

The only variation that I would make to the install procedure is for the
flycircuit package itself, where I would now recommend:

install.packages('natmanager')
natmanager::install(pkgs = 'flycircuit')

Although the original instructions should still be fine and the next
steps remain the same:

if(!require("devtools")) install.packages("devtools")
devtools::source_gist("bbaf5d53353b3944c090")
remotesync(dps,download.missing = TRUE)

With best wishes,

Greg.
